title: Nurturing Our Relations: A Randomized Controlled Trial of Virtual Reality Indigenous Cultural Safety Training Compared to Control for Obstetric and Neonatal Care Nurses
official: Nurturing Our Relations: An RCT of Virtual Reality Indigenous Cultural Safety Training Compared to Control for Obstetric and Neonatal Care Nurses
summary: This study will test a new virtual reality (VR) Indigenous cultural safety training designed for hospital nurses attending births and caring for sick babies. The training (study Arm #1) includes two one-hour sessions that each include a VR encounter with a virtual Indigenous patient. This will compared to two one hour sessions of unrelated online clinical training (study Arm #2). Participant nurses will be randomly put into one of these two study arms. The study team will then assess whether or not the training improved Indigenous patient care outcomes using live Indigenous actors performing as patients. Participating nurses will be scheduled to assess these mock patients 10-12 weeks after their training. The quality of care they provide during these mock patient encounters will be rated using standard scales. They study hypothesis is that nurses who take the virtual reality Indigenous patient encounter training will have better relational engagement and provide higher quality clinical care during the Indigenous standardized patient encounter compared to nurses who were randomized to the unrelated clinical online training.
conditions: Quality of Nursing Care for Indigenous Patients

interventions.name: Virtual Reality Indigenous Cultural Safety Training
Online Clinical Education on non-ICS topic

criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Registered Nurse working in the postpartum, labor and delivery, and/or neonatal care units of St. Michael's Hospital and St. Joseph's hospital in Toronto.
* Stated intention to remain working as a Registered Nurse at either hospital for at least 5 months following completion of the training intervention/control to ensure they are available to complete all necessary assessments for the project.

Exclusion Criteria:

* Indigenous nurses will be excluded from this study, as this study's training and assessment tools have been designed for non-Indigenous participants and evidence suggests that Indigenous participants, who will have experienced anti-Indigenous racism, will benefit from tailored training that protects participants from additional harms from anti-Indigenous racism.
